source: Karpathy AutoResearch — closed-loop ML experiment agent
summary: Karpathy built a closed-loop experiment runner (AutoResearch) that ran 700 ML experiments in two days on a single GPU from a 630-line training script. Advocates agent-native APIs over human UIs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — confirms the value of autonomous looping agents, but AutoResearch is ML-training-focused not orchestration-focused. AgentForge already has auto-dispatch (HID-72) in backlog.

summary: LangMem (MIT, LangChain team) adds semantic, episodic, and procedural memory types to LangGraph agents. MongoDB backend added for LangGraph.js in May 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge does not use LangGraph; skill distillation already covers procedural memory, and HID-188 tracks episodic memory.

summary: Open-source memory system combining short-term, long-term episodic, and profile memory layers. Reports 0.9169 on LoCoMo benchmark with gpt-4.1-mini.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — directly relevant to cross-run episodic memory, but HID-188 already tracks this capability. Backlog also at cap (11 open issues).

source: Mem0 — open-source agent memory library (~54K stars)
summary: Apache 2.0 memory layer for agents supporting semantic fact extraction and episodic storage. Most widely adopted dedicated agent memory library per third-party surveys.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — relevant to HID-188 (run-outcome episodic memory) as a potential implementation reference, but that issue already exists.

summary: Treats tool use under a monetary budget as a sequential decision problem. Uses a learned world model and Monte Carlo lookahead to enforce hard budget feasibility at inference time.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — directly relevant to cost-aware orchestration, but blocked on HID-163 (token telemetry) which must ship first to provide measurement data.

source: BAGEN — agents waste 44% of tokens on tasks they will fail (arXiv May 2026)
summary: Argues that frontier models are over-optimistic about task success, continue spending tokens on likely-to-fail tasks, and that agents should estimate remaining budget mid-run.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — budget awareness is a real gap, but requires HID-163 telemetry as a prerequisite before it can be acted on.

source: Self-improving agent reflection loops — 2026 practitioner survey
summary: Surveys generate-critique-revise reflection loops. Grounded critique (tests, execution) beats naive self-critique. Reports 91% HumanEval pass@1 for Reflexion. Most gains come in first two passes.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge already ships skill distillation as a reflection mechanism. Advanced self-critique is tracked by HID-93 (adversarial plan critique).

source: AutoGen enters maintenance mode / Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA
summary: Microsoft AutoGen is now community-managed and receives no new features; Microsoft Agent Framework hit 1.0 GA in April 2026. LangGraph 1.2.x and CrewAI 1.15.x are the active alternatives.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocess model (Claude Code + Codex), not Python agent frameworks. Framework consolidation is an ecosystem signal, not an actionable gap.

source: Shunyu Yao tau-bench behavioral fingerprinting — 2026 evaluation focus
summary: Yao's current work has shifted from agent reasoning architectures toward evaluation rigor (tau-bench, behavioral fingerprinting of web agents). No new agent architecture paper found in 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — evaluation methodology is interesting but AgentForge already has an acceptance-test harness issue (HID-135). No new actionable architecture.
